transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… I guess I’m here because I keep avoiding the front of the store. Like, the front windows and that part of the street outside—I just can’t make myself go over there anymore. I work retail, so I’m supposed to be out there sometimes, but I keep making excuses to stay in the back.

It’s embarrassing, honestly. I’ll be folding stock or pretending I need to check inventory, even if there’s no real reason. I know that sounds kind of dumb, but I just… I can’t seem to go near that area.
When you avoid the front of the store, do you feel anxious or scared, like you might not be able to get away if you needed to?

Yeah… sort of. I mean, I don’t know if it’s exactly that I think I can’t get away. It’s more like when I even think about going near the front windows, I just freeze up and start looking for any reason not to go.

Like I’ll suddenly decide the stockroom needs organizing, or I’ll tell someone I’m checking inventory, even when it’s not really necessary. And then I feel stupid because it’s literally part of my job to be out there sometimes. I used to complain about customers coming in five minutes before closing—sorry, random—but now I’d almost rather deal with that than have to stand by those windows or that bit of the street outside.
When you feel that freeze or urge to avoid the front of the store, is it because you’re worried something bad might happen to you there, like having a panic attack or feeling trapped?

I don’t know if I’m thinking, like, “I’m going to have a panic attack” exactly. It’s more that I just… can’t make myself go there. Near the front windows, or that stretch of street outside.

I’ll start heading that way and then suddenly I’m like, oh, I should go check something in the back, or I’ll pretend there’s stock to sort. Which is ridiculous because at my job you can’t just live in the stockroom forever. I used to actually like being up front sometimes—well, depending on the music they had playing, because our playlist is awful—but now I just keep finding excuses not to be there.
Is it only the front of the store and that part of the street outside that you avoid, or do you find yourself avoiding other places too for similar reasons?

Mostly it’s just the front of the store and that bit of street outside. Like, I’m not avoiding everywhere, you know? I can still go to other places, run errands and stuff—well, unless it’s somewhere with terrible parking, but that’s a whole separate thing.

It’s really those front windows. I’ll be at work and I’ll realize I’m making up reasons to stay in the back, like pretending inventory needs checking or shelves need sorting, even when they don’t. And I know it’s part of my job to be up there, which makes me feel kind of ridiculous, but I just can’t make myself go near that area.
When you avoid the front of the store and that part of the street, is it because you're worried you won't be able to leave quickly or you might feel trapped if something uncomfortable happens?

Not really like “trapped,” I don’t think. I mean, maybe a little? But it’s not like I’m standing there calculating exits or anything.

It’s more that I just can’t make myself go near the front windows or that part of the street anymore. I’ll come up with any excuse to stay in the back—like, suddenly the shelves need fixing or there’s some box I definitely have to deal with, even if I know I’m kind of making it up. Which is awkward because being up front is literally part of my job, so then I feel like everyone can probably tell I’m avoiding it.

Have you ever had a panic attack or a sudden rush of intense anxiety in places other than the front of the store, or are you worried that you might have one in public and not be able to get help or escape easily?

I don’t think so? Not that I’ve really noticed. I mean, I get stressed in public sometimes, like anyone does, especially if a line is taking forever and someone’s cart is blocking the whole aisle—people do that constantly—but I don’t think I’m walking around worried I’m going to suddenly lose it and need help or not be able to leave.

It’s more tied to that front area, as far as I can tell. But I don’t know, maybe I’m not paying attention to it the right way.
When you’re near the front of the store or that part of the street, do you feel afraid that you might suddenly feel extremely anxious or have a panic attack there?

I’m not sure if I’d call it that. Like, I don’t go up there thinking, “Oh no, I’m going to have a panic attack.” It’s more just… I don’t want to be there, and then I start getting all worked up because I’m there, if that makes sense.

But not like I’m specifically scared of the anxiety itself. I don’t know, maybe that’s splitting hairs. I just know I see the front windows or that stretch outside and my brain kind of goes, “Nope,” and then I suddenly remember I have something very important to do in the back. Which, I mean, sometimes there really is stuff to do back there, but probably not as urgently as I make it sound.

When you’re near the front of the store or that part of the street, do you feel afraid that you might suddenly feel extremely anxious or have physical symptoms like a racing heart or shortness of breath?

I don’t know if I’m afraid of that happening exactly. Like, I’m not standing there thinking, “My heart’s going to start racing,” or “I won’t be able to breathe.” I’m more just… I notice I’m near that spot and then I want to get away from it.

Sometimes I’m so busy trying to look normal that I don’t even know what my body is doing, if that makes sense. Like at work I’ll be pretending to check receipts or straighten something, and then I’m also thinking about whether my manager can tell I’m acting weird, and then I remember I forgot to text my sister back—sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

So, no, I don’t think I’m specifically scared of the physical symptoms. I just don’t like being there.
When you avoid the front of the store, is it more about not wanting to feel anxious or panicky, or is it more about just not wanting to be in that spot regardless of how you feel physically?

It’s more the spot, I think. Like, I don’t go, “I don’t want to feel panicky,” I go, “I can’t be over there.” The front windows, that part of the street outside… I just keep finding reasons to be in the back instead.

Which is stupid because that’s part of my job, you know? Like if someone needs help up front, I’ll suddenly decide the stockroom needs fixing, or I’ll tell myself I should check something in back. And sometimes the back really is a mess, honestly, people just shove things anywhere, but… yeah. It’s mostly I don’t want to be in that spot.
Have you ever had similar feelings of avoidance in other places or situations, or is this something that only happens at the front of the store and that part of the street outside?

Mostly it’s just that area. The front of the store, especially the windows, and then that same stretch of street outside. That’s what I came in about, really, because I can’t seem to make myself go over there anymore without making up some reason to be in the back.

Like I’ll suddenly “need” to check stock or fix shelves or look for something that probably doesn’t even matter right then. And I know it sounds kind of ridiculous because it’s literally part of my job to be up front sometimes, but my brain just keeps steering me away from it.

Other places… I mean, I don’t think it’s like everywhere. It’s that spot. That whole front area.
When you’re near the front of the store or that part of the street, do you worry that you’ll suddenly feel intense anxiety or have a panic attack there?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’m standing there thinking, like, “I’m going to have a panic attack right here.” It’s more that I notice where I am and my head kind of goes, nope, not here.

But then I also start thinking about whether people can tell I’m acting strange, like customers or my manager, and then I’ll get distracted by trying to look busy, which is what I do at work anyway. So I don’t know if that counts as worrying about anxiety happening. It feels more like I just don’t want to be in that exact place.
